nary_nodes.label: Workers use AI on job
evidence: About 55% of workers say they use AI on the job

nary_nodes.label: AI cuts task time by 1-2 hours
evidence: about one-third of those reporting it cuts the time they need to complete a given assignment by one to two hours

nary_nodes.label: Workers use AI for specific tasks
evidence: Workers reported turning to AI for help with tasks including writing, generating new ideas, conducting research and completing administrative tasks.

nary_nodes.label: Smaller share uses AI for other tasks
evidence: A smaller share of workers use it to write code, for medical care and to manage logistics or supply chains

nary_nodes.label: AI shaves less than an hour
evidence: One-quarter of employees who reported using AI at work say the tools shaved less than an hour off the time it would otherwise have taken them to complete a task

nary_nodes.label: AI cuts workloads by three hours
evidence: A smaller share, at 15%, of workers saw even greater efficiency gains, saying that AI cut their workloads by three hours per task.

nary_nodes.label: AI saves four hours
evidence: An additional 15% said it saved them four hours.
A smaller share, at 15%, of workers saw even greater efficiency gains, saying that AI cut their workloads by three hours per task. An additional 15% said it saved them four hours.

nary_nodes.label: AI adoption decreases productivity
evidence: Research from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology shows that AI adoption in manufacturing initially decreases productivity before ultimately helping workers achieve long-term gains.

nary_nodes.label: J-curve explains productivity phenomenon
evidence: Economists use the "J-curve" model to explain the phenomenon.
